Good. Now let me check for updates to the remaining three sources: Palmer 2020 (sexual and reproductive health, CD013680), Ames 2019 (qualitative synthesis, CD013680), and Khormi 2026 (Cureus).
Now let me check whether the Agarwal 2021 decision-support review (CD012944) has been updated, and also check the WHO 2019 guideline and Marcolino 2018 for updates.

I now have enough information to compile the full assessment. Let me summarize what I found for each source:

**[1] Agarwal 2025 (CD012925.pub2)** — Published April 7, 2025. This IS the pub2 update. The draft correctly cites it as "2025." CURRENT — confirmed as the latest version.

**[2] Agarwal 2021 (CD012944.pub2)** — Published July 27, 2021. No pub3 found anywhere; the 2025 Agarwal review (CD012925) cites it as "Agarwal 2021" without superseding it. No update found. UNKNOWN — cannot positively confirm it is still the latest (no pub3 found, but also no positive confirmation it hasn't been updated since my searches only show the 2021 version being cited).

**[3] Palmer 2020 (CD013679)** — Published July 14, 2020. No update found. UNKNOWN.

**[4] Palmer 2020 (CD013680)** — Published July 14, 2020. No update found. UNKNOWN.

**[5] Ames 2019 (CD013447)** — Published 2019. No update found. UNKNOWN.

**[6] WHO 2019 guideline** — The 2019 guideline remains the current version; a planned update was noted but no new version found. UNKNOWN (cannot positively confirm no update exists).

**[7] Marcolino 2018** — Not held; draft explicitly notes it could not be held. Not assessed.

**[8] Khormi 2026 (Cureus)** — Published May 7, 2026. Confirmed as the current publication. CURRENT.

Now, critically: the draft cites [1] as "Agarwal S, Chin WY, Vasudevan L, et al. 2025" — this matches CD012925.pub2, April 2025. CURRENT. The draft cites [2] as "Agarwal S, Glenton C, Tamrat T, et al. 2021" — this is CD012944.pub2, July 2021. No pub3 found. For [3] and [4], both Palmer 2020 reviews — no updates found. For [5] Ames 2019 — no update found. For [6] WHO 2019 — no update found.

I found no other objections. The quotations on provider adherence (2 studies, 185 participants), the authors' conclusions, the eight-study count, and the "systems lens" sentence all match the review. The "no studies reported" outcomes and the smoking and systolic blood pressure results also match it.
